title: A graph convolution layer and message passing
hints: Add self-loops first: A_tilde = A + I. Degrees d = A_tilde.sum(1). Then A_hat = A_tilde * d[:, None] ** -0.5 * d[None, :] ** -0.5, which is D^-1/2 A_tilde D^-1/2 without building a diagonal matrix.
A GCN layer is two matrix products: A_hat @ (X @ W) + b, then the activation. Row i of A_hat @ (X W) is the degree-normalized sum of the messages X_j W from i's neighbors and itself.

Permutation equivariance comes for free if every operation is either per-node (X @ W, activation) or aggregation through A_hat: relabeling nodes permutes both A_hat's rows and columns and X's rows, so the output rows are permuted the same way. Mean pooling over rows then makes the readout invariant.
